description: Operational health of KI Norge in PROD and TT02. Availability comes from the blackbox-exporter HTTP probes of the public Astro frontends (ki.norge.no, ki.test.norge.no) in admin-prod-obs-amw; traffic, latency, errors and dependencies come from the headless Umbraco CMS behind them (Application Insights, dis-core-{prod,tt02}-products-ai, cloud_RoleName=kinorgeportal). Both environments are queried in a single cross-resource target and told apart by _ResourceId, so there is no environment variable to switch. Unlike info.altinn.no there is no deep /health probe — ki.norge.no does not expose one — so availability here means 'the site answered HTTP 200', not 'the app reported itself healthy'. Datasource UIDs are pinned rather than templated so the panels cannot silently bind to the wrong datasource.
title: KI Norge — Service Health

Probe right now

panels.description: Both hosts sit behind Cloudflare, so this is Cloudflare's edge certificate and normally renews itself. A number falling below ~14 days without recovering is worth chasing.

panels.description: Slowest of the two IP families, per host. Baseline is roughly 0.1–0.4 s from the admin-prod-aks probers.

panels.title: Probe status over time — PROD and TT02, IPv4 and IPv6
panels.description: The panel the Slack availability alert links to. The alert collapses these four series into one and fires only when all of them are down, so this is where you see whether an incident was one IP family or the whole site. Job names are matched exactly here rather than by regex — Azure Managed Prometheus does not anchor `=~`, so a loose matcher would pull in the unrelated `-health-check` and `-kuberneteswrapper` jobs.

panels.title: Probe duration by host and IP family
panels.description: Splits what the stat above collapses. A gap here means the probe failed rather than returned slowly.

panels.title: Environment scorecard (selected range)

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
let reqs = requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize
    Requests = count(),
    Ok       = countif(toint(resultCode) between (200 .. 399)),
    Err5xx   = countif(toint(resultCode) >= 500),
    NotFound = countif(toint(resultCode) == 404),
    P95ms    = round(percentile(iff(not(name has_any ("serverEventHub", "PreviewHub")) and toint(resultCode) != 404, duration, real(null)), 95), 1)
  by Env;
let errs = traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal" and severityLevel >= 3
| where not(tostring(customDimensions.['message_template.text']) startswith "uSync-import ENDRET skjema")
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize Errors = count() by Env;
reqs
| join kind=leftouter errs on Env
| extend Errors = coalesce(Errors, 0)
| extend
    Err5xxPct   = round(100.0 * Err5xx / Requests, 3),
    NotFoundPct = round(100.0 * NotFound / Requests, 1)
| extend EnvOrder = case(Env == "TT02", 1, Env == "PROD", 2, 9)
| project EnvOrder, Env, Requests, Ok, Err5xx, Err5xxPct, Errors, NotFound, NotFoundPct, P95ms
| order by EnvOrder asc
| project-away EnvOrder

panels.description: One row per environment, for the CMS backend behind the probed frontend. `Errors` counts severity>=3 traces with the routine uSync schema-import notices filtered out — the exact population the exception alert rules fire on. `NotFound` is reported apart from `Err5xx` because 404s are ~94% of all traffic here (almost all of it bot scanning) and would otherwise swamp the real error signal. `P95ms` excludes both 404s and the Umbraco SignalR long-poll hubs.

panels.title: P95 latency (404s and SignalR long-poll excluded)

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal" and toint(resultCode) != 404
| where not(name has_any ("serverEventHub", "PreviewHub"))
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize P95ms = round(percentile(duration, 95), 1) by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Env
| order by timestamp asc

panels.description: `/umbraco/serverEventHub` and `/umbraco/PreviewHub` are SignalR streams held open for minutes to hours by design — leaving them in takes the observed max from ~3 s to ~2.2 h and makes every latency reading meaningless. 404s are excluded too; they never reach application code.

panels.title: Not found (404) — 94% of all requests; only one slice is actionable
404s by category
panels.description: Both environments combined, split by what the caller was after. **Scanner probe** is internet background noise (`/wp-login.php`, `/.env.*`, `/actuator/env`) and needs no action. **Crawler / browser asset** is `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, `favicon.ico` and friends — worth fixing once, cosmetically. **Content or API miss** is a real request to `/umbraco/...` that found nothing, and is the only band that should ever prompt work.

panels.title: Content and API misses — the actionable 404s

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal" and toint(resultCode) == 404
| where name has "/umbraco/"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize Count = count(), LastSeen = max(timestamp) by Env, Endpoint = name
| project Env, Endpoint, Count, LastSeen
| order by Count desc
| take 30

panels.description: A 404 on the Umbraco Delivery API means the Astro frontend at ki.norge.no asked for content that is not published. Usually a broken content reference or a page unpublished without a redirect. Empty is the healthy state.

panels.title: Top scanner probes (noise — shown so it can be recognised, not acted on)

azureLogAnalytics.query:
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal" and toint(resultCode) == 404
| where not(name has "/umbraco/")
| where not(name has_any ("robots.txt", "sitemap.xml", "favicon.ico", "apple-touch-icon", ".well-known"))
| summarize Count = count(), Callers = dcount(client_IP) by Path = name
| project Path, Count, Callers
| order by Count desc
| take 25

panels.description: Commodity vulnerability scanning against a host that runs none of the software being probed. Listed here so a spike in the 404 chart can be dismissed quickly. If this ever becomes expensive, the fix is a WAF rule upstream, not application code.

panels.title: Endpoints — volume, outcome and latency

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
requests
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| extend Endpoint = replace_regex(name, @"/[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}", "/{guid}")
| summarize
    Count  = count(),
    Ok     = countif(toint(resultCode) between (200 .. 399)),
    NotFound = countif(toint(resultCode) == 404),
    Err5xx = countif(toint(resultCode) >= 500),
    P95ms  = round(percentile(iff(not(name has_any ("serverEventHub", "PreviewHub")), duration, real(null)), 95), 1),
    P99ms  = round(percentile(iff(not(name has_any ("serverEventHub", "PreviewHub")), duration, real(null)), 99), 1)
  by Env, Endpoint
| extend OkPct = round(100.0 * Ok / Count, 1)
| project Env, Endpoint, Count, OkPct, NotFound, Err5xx, P95ms, P99ms
| order by Count desc
| take 40

panels.description: GUIDs are normalised to `{guid}` so the Delivery API item route collapses into one row instead of thousands. Latency percentiles null out the SignalR long-poll hubs rather than filtering the rows, so their request counts still show. Sort by P99ms to find slow endpoints.

panels.title: Logs — the same grouping the alert rules use
Trace volume by severity

azureLogAnalytics.query:
traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal"
| extend Severity = case(
    severityLevel >= 4, "4 Critical",
    severityLevel == 3, "3 Error",
    severityLevel == 2, "2 Warning",
    severityLevel == 1, "1 Information",
    "0 Verbose")
| summarize Count = count() by bin(timestamp, $__interval), Severity
| order by timestamp asc

panels.description: Both environments combined. Severity 3 and 4 are what the alert rules watch; note that the uSync schema-import notices are logged at severity 3 despite being routine, which is why the rules filter them out by message template.

panels.title: Errors the alerts fire on (Type / Details / Count)

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal"
| where severityLevel >= 3
| where not(tostring(customDimensions.['message_template.text']) startswith "uSync-import ENDRET skjema")
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| extend ExType = tostring(customDimensions.['exception.type'])
| extend ExMsg = tostring(customDimensions.['exception.message'])
| extend Details = iff(isnotempty(ExMsg), ExMsg, message)
| summarize Count = count() by Env, Type = ExType, Details = substring(Details, 0, 200)
| project Env, Type, Details, Count
| order by Count desc
| take 30

panels.description: Byte-for-byte the grouping in `rules-exceptions.yaml`, so a Slack alert can be matched to a row here. Each row in the alert query becomes its own alert instance, with `Type` and `Details` riding along as labels into the Slack message.

panels.title: Suppressed by the alert filter — uSync schema-import notices

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
traces
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal"
| where severityLevel >= 3
| where not(not(tostring(customDimensions.['message_template.text']) startswith "uSync-import ENDRET skjema"))
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize Count = count(), LastSeen = max(timestamp) by Env, Summary = tostring(customDimensions.Summary)
| project Env, Summary, Count, LastSeen
| order by Count desc
| take 20

panels.description: Umbraco's uSync logs "skjema ENDRET" at severity 3 (`Log4NetLevel: ERROR`) on every content-type sync, which is routine. The alert rules exclude it by message template so the Slack channel stays trustworthy — it is surfaced here so the suppression is visible rather than silent. A sustained rise means the deployed uSync files disagree with the database and is worth a look, just not a page.

panels.title: Dependencies by target

azureLogAnalytics.query:
let envOf = (r: string) { case(
    r has "dis-core-tt02", "TT02",
    r has "dis-core-prod", "PROD",
    "unknown") };
dependencies
| where cloud_RoleName == "kinorgeportal"
| extend Env = envOf(_ResourceId)
| summarize
    Count  = count(),
    Failed = countif(success == false),
    P95ms  = round(percentile(duration, 95), 1)
  by Env, Type = type, Target = target
| extend FailPct = round(100.0 * Failed / Count, 2)
| project Env, Type, Target, Count, Failed, FailPct, P95ms
| order by Count desc
| take 30

panels.description: Everything here is currently `InProc` SignalR hub lifecycle — this CMS makes no outbound HTTP or SQL calls that App Insights records. A new `HTTP` or `SQL` row appearing is a change in the service's shape and worth knowing about.
